newsitem.title: UK: Bulgarian Bradys "big buy" -- Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Bradys "big buy" -- Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Morgan Stanley said it was revising its medium term outlook on Bulgaria to overweight from neutral and said Bulgarian Brady prices have at least five points of upside over the next two months.

In a research note dated February 7, emerging markets debt analyst Eric Fine said a political resolution of recent turmoil had now occured and he expected an effective temporary government to be established under Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski.
The ruling Socialists earlier this month agreed to hold early elections on April 20 after 30 days of mass protests. A caretaker cabinet is expected to be appointed this week.
"We believe that April elections will result in a pro-reform coalition government that will be able to cement a currency board and other reforms," the note said.
It said there were near-term risks, mostly involving obstructionism by the ruling BSP, but these would offer the opportunity to take advantage of any related price weakness.
Also, the IMF could choose to wait for the results of early elections before final agreement on new lending, although this was not the official position.

It said the selection of a temporary government, which could bring in key reforms such as a currency board, could result in spread of 910 basis points on Bulgarian IAB bonds, representing a price target of 58 from a current 53.
"Moreover, we believe that a victory by the reformist opposition in mid-April should precipitate further tightening to spreads of roughly 704 bp."
Follow-on policies from a future government by about mid-year should result in further tightening, possibly by another 100 bp. This represents a price target of 70.5.
